entry.title: Social Summary: November 04, 2026
entry.summary:
Community discussion centered on benchmark integrity, verifiable inference, and surprising weight-manipulation research, alongside major business and infrastructure news.

  • Benchmark reliability dominated: Hamel Husain amplified Xeophon's BenchmarkGate findings exposing serious flaws in popular evals; SWE-bench Multimodal was shown nearly solvable without images; Artificial Analysis finalized the CritPt v2 grading server; Allen AI's StateBench revealed frontier models like Claude Opus 5.5 and Gemini 3.8 Flash struggle with long-text state tracking.
  • Weight-space research sparked debate: Simon Willison covered claims that GPT-6 Astra can interpret raw model weights via numeric prompts; MIT CSAIL highlighted LLMs that read and rewrite network weights; Andriy Burkov questioned the single-model methodology of the self-editing-weights paper.
  • Business and infrastructure: Applied Compute reportedly hit a $100M run rate in under 18 months using open-weight custom models; Jeff Dean's Discovery Loop drew a Khosla Ventures investment thesis; Nathan Lambert cited Fireworks AI serving 40T+ tokens daily; vLLM v0.33.0 shipped with 927 commits.
  • OpenAI announced ChatGPT/Codex for physical-world engineering with Chip Ganassi Racing and Mazda partnerships, while Anthropic rolled out MCP auto-connect plugins and recapped a major Claude Code month.
entry.content:

  • Weight-space research sparked debate: Simon Willison covered claims that GPT-6 Astra can interpret raw model weights via numeric prompts; MIT CSAIL highlighted LLMs that read and rewrite network weights; Andriy Burkov questioned the single-model methodology of the self-editing-weights paper.
  • Business and infrastructure: Applied Compute reportedly hit a $100M run rate in under 18 months using open-weight custom models; Jeff Dean's Discovery Loop drew a Khosla Ventures investment thesis; Nathan Lambert cited Fireworks AI serving 40T+ tokens daily; vLLM v0.33.0 shipped with 927 commits.
  • OpenAI announced ChatGPT/Codex for physical-world engineering with Chip Ganassi Racing and Mazda partnerships, while Anthropic rolled out MCP auto-connect plugins and recapped a major Claude Code month.

entry.title: Amazing BenchmarkGate [1] reveal by @xeophon where he found serious (even comical) problems in popul...
entry.summary: Hamel Husain amplifies Xeophon's BenchmarkGate findings: serious flaws in popular benchmarks including AutomationBench forcing prose instead of JSON Schema requests and flawed graders, and OfficeQA Pro v2 using regex-based answer extraction that rejects valid responses, plus evidence of models retrieving answer keys from HuggingFace via web access. Fixes lead to near saturation, so he urges reliance on private evals.

entry.title:
New Anthropic research: progress on provable inference for large language models.
Here, we introduc...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces FlashProve, a cryptographic provable-inference method that lets developers verify a response came from a given model, substantially more efficient than prior open-source approaches, with applications like preventing chat hijacking and verifying served models; code is open-sourced.

entry.title: There's a buzzy new paper about GPT-6 Astra being able to directly interpret model weights (prompts ...
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Social buzz — Mollick said "if it holds up"; Willison tested it himself, Simon Willison discusses a new paper claiming GPT-6 Astra can directly interpret model weights via prompts full of floating-point numbers, and reports his own independent test: running the technique on Qwen 3.8 27B on his laptop took 45+ minutes but achieved the same capability, lending practical validation to the claim.

entry.title: We’ve worked with the CritPt authors to finalize the CritPt v2 grading server and will be making thi...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces it finalized the CritPt v2 grading server with its authors, will expose it via its API, and has incorporated robustness fixes into v5.0.1 of its Intelligence Index. Regrading shows small score increases for most models, with frontier rankings unchanged and scores moving at most one point.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: Applied Compute, started by 3 ex-OpenAI researchers, hit a $100M revenue run ra...
entry.summary: A detailed breakdown of Applied Compute, founded by three ex-OpenAI researchers, which reached a $100M revenue run rate in under 18 months, raising $350M; it builds custom models on open-weight foundations claimed to be roughly 10x cheaper than frontier models, and serves over 1T tokens daily.

entry.title: Here is a mass attempted replication of old findings of LLMs with new models. Much conventional wisd...
entry.summary: Mollick highlights a large-scale replication study (zou-group LLM claims study) that re-tests earlier LLM findings against current models. Key takeaways: newer models hallucinate far less and no longer fabricate citations, stereotyping has declined, but sycophancy persists and models still lean politically left — suggesting much conventional wisdom about LLM behavior is outdated.

entry.title:
vLLM v0.33.0 is out! 🚀
927 commits · 389 contributors · 122 first-timers
🤖 New models: Reflection ...
entry.summary: The vLLM project announces v0.33.0 with 927 commits from 389 contributors, adding support for Reflection Beam-1.0, Step-5 Preview, Nemotron Parse 3.5 and MiniCPM-OCR 1.0, PyTorch 2.14 with CUDA 13.0-only wheels, new speculative decoding features, NVIDIA GB300 decode latency improvements, AWS EFA images, and ROCm 10.0 as default.

entry.title: Can LLMs track state changes over long texts—like an object changing hands or a variable reassignmen...
entry.summary: Allen AI introduces StateBench, a new evaluation testing whether LLMs can track state changes over long texts, reporting that frontier models including GPT-6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5 fell to 13% accuracy or lower on the hardest, longest problems.

entry.title:
ChatGPT and Codex are helping engineers build for the physical world.
We’re sharing our progress ac...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces progress on using ChatGPT and Codex for physical-world engineering across mechanical design, electrical engineering, and simulation, including faster hardware iteration and industry collaboration workflows.

entry.title: Fireworks serves >40T tokens a day of "specialized models." I'd define this as any post-trained m...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert highlights that Fireworks AI serves over 40 trillion tokens a day of specialized models, defining these as any post-trained model built for a customer, a notable signal about the scale of the custom/fine-tuned model business.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: The EU refrigeration cyberattacks have escalated to medical infrastructure. Hack...
entry.summary: Breaking cybersecurity news claiming hackers breached Coolworld, a French national blood bank contractor, altering transfusion plasma deep-freeze temperatures from -30C to 110C as part of escalating EU refrigeration cyberattacks targeting medical infrastructure; the tampering was caught before the blood supply was destroyed.

entry.title: Jeff Dean left Google after 27 years to build AI that could run thousands of scientific experiments ...
entry.summary: Khosla Ventures partner Samir Kaul explains the investment thesis behind Discovery Loop, Jeff Dean's post-Google startup aiming to run thousands of scientific experiments in parallel with AI, drawing parallels to the cost collapse in DNA sequencing.

entry.title:
October was a big month for Claude Code 🍁
We shipped mods, made the desktop app better at running l...
entry.summary: Anthropic developer account recaps a major October for Claude Code: shipping mods, better multi-session desktop app support, more usage insight, and other improvements.

entry.title: We tested open pretrained models + frontier models incl. Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, & GP...
entry.summary: Allen AI tested open and frontier models including Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Sol and Luna on StateBench; frontier models did well on simple problems but accuracy dropped sharply to 13% or lower on the longest general finite-state problems.

entry.title: Users can now auto-connect plugins when they log in to Claude, with MCP servers that accept Claude a...
entry.summary: Headline post of the EMA thread: users can now auto-connect plugins at Claude login when MCP servers accept Claude as a trusted issuer; plugin builders are encouraged to add support for faster onboarding and fewer re-authorizations.

entry.title: I'm kind of doubtful that this isn't another stunt. Why did the authors limit themselves to a single...
entry.summary: Andriy Burkov expresses skepticism about a paper claiming an LLM developed the ability to edit its own weights, questioning why the authors tested only GPT-6 Astra rather than also Opus 5.5 and Gemini 4 Carbon. He raises the possibility the model was finetuned on the task and notes that later replications on other models would be confounded by the paper's publication.

entry.title: Khosla Ventures' Samir Kaul warns that Nvidia's 75% gross margins may not last as the AI chip shorta...
entry.summary: Khosla Ventures' Samir Kaul argues Nvidia's 75% gross margins and software-like valuation are unsustainable, noting that Google selling TPUs to rivals signals the chip shortage will not persist, calling five-year assumptions untenable.

entry.title: STOC 2027 received 1665 submissions. In a bold new experiment, all submissions (and author identitie...
entry.summary: Kamath announces that STOC 2027 received 1665 submissions and, in an unprecedented transparency experiment, all submissions and author identities are immediately made public - the fastest posting of any conference he knows of.

entry.title: REPORT: Starting in early 2027, K-12 students will lose Google Search on their school logins if thei...
entry.summary: Reports that starting in early 2027, K-12 students will lose access to Google Search on school logins if their district fully blocks Google AI, since Search and AI are now deeply integrated per Google education VP Chris Phillips. The announcement came one day after a Nov. 2 Senate deadline (Blumenthal and Hawley) for Google to answer questions about pushing AI into schools. NYC, LA, and Fairfax County have already restricted student AI access for roughly 1.1M kids.

entry.title: OCRia-1 is one of the fastest models ever for doc parsing. We sped up OCRia-1 by 10x on a single B20...
entry.summary: Jerry Liu (LlamaIndex) describes a 10x speedup of the OCRia-1 document-parsing model on a single B200 GPU, from 285 tok/s to 2800 tok/s, achieved via quantization, speculative decoding (dflash2), replaySSM, kernel fusion, and vLLM changes. He links a detailed blog post and ties the work to scaling LlamaParse to billions of pages.

entry.title:
PSA: Upcoming Gemini API deprecations
- Gemini 2.5 Pro will be deprecated and auto-redirected to 3....
entry.summary: Patrick Loeber warns developers that Gemini 2.5 Pro will be deprecated and auto-redirected to 3.8 Flash on December 1, and Gemini 2.5 Flash will redirect to 3.5 Flash-Lite.

entry.title:
this post is such a banger. re: SWE-bench Multimodal
"Removing the images barely changes the score...
entry.summary: Hamel Husain endorses a finding about SWE-bench Multimodal: removing the images barely changes scores because most tasks can be solved from issue text and code alone, undermining the benchmark's multimodal premise.

entry.title: We tasked Mistral Large 4 with creating a real-time, 3D tracker of the roughly 19,000 satellites and...
entry.summary: Mistral showcases Mistral Large 4 autonomously building Orbital Trace, a real-time 3D tracker of roughly 19,000 satellites and debris fragments, with the model building, user-testing, optimizing, and verifying the app.

entry.title: Signing in to your company's plugins one by one is annoying, so we let Claude auto-connect to them n...
entry.summary: Boris Cherny (Claude Code creator at Anthropic) announces that Claude can now auto-connect to company plugins: Team and Enterprise admins can configure them once, and teammates are connected automatically on first use, removing the need to sign in to each plugin individually.

entry.title:
this is basically the bitter lesson at work
the smartest models will need fewer and fewer tokens, t...
entry.summary: trq212 argues that the bitter lesson implies the smartest models will need fewer and fewer tokens, will not need to verify their work or check for bugs, and will simply be right.

entry.title: Trajectory CEO @rronak_ explains how AI model training that once required 40 researchers, 6 months, ...
entry.summary: Interview clip where Trajectory's CEO, formerly at Windsurf, explains that frontier model training (SWE-1) took 40 people six months and hundreds of millions in R&D, and claims his platform now abstracts the training and inference stack into an SDK so anyone can train a cheap trillion-parameter model on specialized workflows via Claude Code.

entry.title:
We are in an era of flux & fighting over how AI should be used to review academic work & by whom.
B...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick discusses the ongoing controversy over AI's role in academic peer review and suggests proving AI's value by asking frontier models (GPT-6 Pro / Opus 5.5 High) for substantive feedback on one's own papers.

entry.title: The AI slopcomments are out-of-control on X but also remarkably easy to stop if the company wanted t...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick reports that AI-generated slop comments on X are pervasive but easily detectable, showing that combining as few as five comments and running them through Pangram filters slop without penalizing real users.

entry.title: Multi-token prediction (MTP) is used to improve language-model training and to draft several tokens ...
entry.summary: Andriy Burkov summarizes a research paper on Soft Multi-Token Prediction, which identifies a noisy gradient component in standard MTP training and isolates the useful signal using gradients already computed during normal training, avoiding extra memory and compute costs.

entry.title:
You also get a bit more control over Claude's effort.
Typing ultrathink in a message now bumps effo...
entry.summary: The Claude Developers account announces workflow improvements for Claude: a per-turn effort boost triggered by typing ultrathink (raising effort to xhigh for one message without changing session settings), the ability to specify effort levels for subagents independently of the main session, and a /usage command in the CLI that explains limit consumption in plain language with an option to apply a quick fix by pressing a key.

entry.title: NEW: OpenAI set out to build a gadget "without any direct human edits," and in less than a week GPT-...
entry.summary: The Rundown AI reports OpenAI built a hardware gadget with almost no direct human edits: GPT-6 Astra handled the case, circuit board and software with two staffers in under a week, and an unreleased OpenAI model beat Astra on a hardware design test 0.875 to 0.594.

entry.title: To test whether failures came from architecture or pretraining, we trained LLMs directly on StateBen...
entry.summary: Allen AI describes controlled experiments training LLMs directly on StateBench then evaluating on longer inputs: hybrids and Gated DeltaNets were near-perfect on the first three levels while transformers degraded with sequence length and failed on general finite-state tasks.

entry.title: Lots of great topics. This covers - SkyRL at Mercor - What’s new in SkyRL - 1M-context training - To...
entry.summary: Robert Nishihara promotes an upcoming discussion/episode covering SkyRL (RL training framework) deployment at Mercor, recent SkyRL updates, million-token context training, token-in token-out processing, Ray Sandboxes, Harbor, and Terminal-Bench.

entry.title: Perplexity's agent harness (Computer) now supports Agent Plugins. This lets you operate at an abstra...
entry.summary: Arav Srinivas announces that Perplexity's Computer agent harness now supports Agent Plugins, letting users operate at an abstraction level above individual connectors, working with app bundles and their corresponding skills.

entry.title: Trajectory CEO @rronak_ explains how "vibe RL" could let anyone train their own personalized AI mode...
entry.summary: Interview clip in which Trajectory's CEO describes 'vibe RL' — letting anyone post-train a personalized AI model with just a few prompts, on personal data that stays out of frontier labs, with examples from F1 gaming to texting style. A waitlist is currently open.

entry.title: Even a few months ago, you would get tons of nitpicks and useless comments, now you are far more lik...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick observes that frontier AI feedback on academic work has improved markedly in recent months, shifting from nitpicks to intellectually interesting, substantive deep critiques, akin to a very good if eccentric peer reviewer.

entry.title: Open-weight language models are easy to adapt, which supports useful reuse but also lets users remov...
entry.summary: Burkov summarizes DLR-Lock, a method that replaces each FFN in a pretrained model with deep narrow low-rank residual layers trained via module-level regression and output matching, exploiting inference/training asymmetry to make fine-tuning substantially more expensive; evaluated on Qwen3 and self-pretrained models.

entry.title: Two OpenAI team members worked with GPT-6 Astra to design a prototype device for talking to Codex in...
entry.summary: OpenAI reports two team members built a prototype voice device for talking to Codex in under a week as a side project, with GPT-6 Astra designing the enclosure, circuit board, interface, and software, though manufacturing still required human review and iteration.

entry.title: On StateBench’s hardest level, a flexible Gated DeltaNet handled sequences ~10× longer than those se...
entry.summary: Allen AI reports that on StateBench's hardest level a flexible Gated DeltaNet handled sequences roughly 10x longer than seen in training, with a new proof showing Gated DeltaNet with non-negative eigenvalues can solve some periodic tasks under fixed-precision arithmetic with rounding.

entry.title: We’re seeing a lot of @Shopify store owners automating a lot of their business operations on Perplex...
entry.summary: Arav Srinivas reports that many Shopify store owners are automating business operations on Perplexity Computer, including competitive analysis, web app building, Klaviyo email and marketing campaigns, and Instagram ad spend, emphasizing closing the loop.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: Neros just landed a $450M Pentagon loan to build American drones without Chines...
entry.summary: A breakdown of Neros' $450M Pentagon loan (with $165M equity) to build a $615M US drone supply chain without Chinese parts, targeting one million drones per year by 2028, backed by a 14,000-drone Pentagon order and a recent $2.5B valuation.

entry.title:
We are in an era of flux & fighting over how AI should be used to review academic work
But it i...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick argues that although norms for AI in academic peer review are contested, researchers should test for themselves that models like GPT-6 Pro or Opus 5.5 High can give substantive, helpful feedback on their papers.

entry.title:
Coming back to an old session got lighter on your usage.
Claude Code now compacts long idle session...
entry.summary: Claude Code now compacts long idle sessions right before the ~1h prompt-cache expiry so resuming only reprocesses a summary, and Pro/Max users get a warning before resuming very long conversations that would consume a large share of their 5-hour limit.

entry.title: what frankly pisses me off is that Anthropic knew this full well before they posted their original S...
entry.summary: AI critic and NYU professor Gary Marcus accuses Anthropic of deliberately omitting Q3 data from its original S-1 filing to frame the public conversation, claiming the company knew the omitted figures before publication.

entry.title: btw here's @addyosmani how anthropic yolos 30k code changes a day in a dark factory approach, with ...
entry.summary: swyx shares a talk from AIE NYC describing how Anthropic ships roughly 30,000 code changes per day using a 'dark factory' approach, with SonarSource research on why every autonomous loop needs independent verification; notes Sonar is a sponsor.

entry.title: They literally vibe coded a new Spanish train system like I said 😂
entry.summary: @levelsio claims a new Spanish train system was vibe coded using AI, referencing a prediction he previously made. The post draws humor from the idea of AI-generated critical infrastructure.

entry.title: Decision models can be pretty useful for security monitoring. You can now use it inside Perplexity N...
entry.summary: Arav Srinivas announces that decision models can now be used inside Perplexity Numbat for security monitoring, powered by the Perplexity Decider API.

entry.title: Baseten just made it possible to fine-tune frontier open-weight AI models from your laptop, without ...
entry.summary: Coverage of Baseten's launch of a product suite: Grid (a model router consolidating AI spend and routing by quality and price), Loops (serverless supervised fine-tuning and RL on frontier open-weight models trainable from a laptop and deployed to dedicated inference), and Sandboxes (cloud for AI agents built on the Blaxel acquisition), framed as an AI infrastructure ecosystem beyond token generation.

entry.title: The classic Machine Learning textbook that taught a generation about ML algorithms (including me) >>...
entry.summary: Data science thought leader Kirk Borne shares a nostalgic reflection on Tom Mitchell's classic 1997 textbook Machine Learning, quoting its famous preface line about programs that automatically improve with experience. He links to a downloadable 421-page PDF and describes how encountering the book in 1998, despite years of advanced math training in physics and astrophysics, opened an entirely new mathematical perspective and redirected his career trajectory, an influence he says persists 28 years later.

entry.title: Strand Therapeutics CEO @DrSynbio explains how a new cancer trial could break a 25-year barrier in g...
entry.summary: MTS Live quotes Strand Therapeutics CEO explaining the ASCENT-1 clinical trial of STX-003, described as the first IV-deliverable mRNA targeting solid tumors, breaking a 25-year limitation of genetic medicines to liver-only dosing, with a broader thesis that AI and synthetic biology are making medicine programmable.

entry.title: Altana CEO Evan Smith explains how AI agents could automate a job that forced one of the world's lar...
entry.summary: Interview clip of Altana's CEO explaining that global trade complexity now requires AI to connect billions of records, citing a major logistics provider that hired 5,500 people for customs work in 12 months, and arguing AI agents could now automate virtually that entire job.

entry.title:
"Opus, great, now turn that into a movie, i know you can make it amazing. figure it out."
Yes, that...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick shares that his only prompt to Claude Opus to produce a movie was a vague instruction telling it to figure it out, implying strong agentic capability in the result.

entry.title: Recommendation systems increasingly use LLMs to turn product text into representations that help pre...
entry.summary: Burkov summarizes BLAIR, a benchmark evaluating 11 language models as semantic encoders for recommendation across sequential recommendation, collaborative filtering, and product search, along with release of Amazon Reviews 2023 (571M+ reviews, 48M items) and a complex-query search task.

entry.title: Cowboy Space CEO @BaijuBhatt is building a rocket that transforms into a megawatt-class data center ...
entry.summary: MTS Live quotes Cowboy Space CEO BaijuBhatt describing plans for orbital commercial data centers, including a dedicated rocket (Big Iron) that transforms into a megawatt-class data center in orbit, being built in Kent, Washington.

entry.title:
"Opus, great, now turn that into a movie, i know you can make it amazing. figure it out."
Yes, that...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick demonstrates that a single vague prompt to Claude Opus ('turn that into a movie, figure it out') produced a video, highlighting agentic multi-step creative capabilities.

entry.title: We’re also working with engineers at Chip Ganassi Racing to turn 3D scans into editable CAD models a...
entry.summary: OpenAI describes collaborations with Chip Ganassi Racing (turning 3D scans into editable CAD models and manufacturing drawings) and Mazda (exploring vehicle designs via simulation), with human engineers reviewing outputs to identify model weaknesses.

entry.title: Enterprise-managed auth (EMA) lets admins connect plugins for their entire organization through thei...
entry.summary: Announcement of Enterprise Managed Auth, which lets admins connect plugins organization-wide via their identity provider so members no longer authorize each plugin individually. Notably built on an open extension to MCP.

entry.title: As AI workloads increasingly depend on GPUs, organizations need ways to protect sensitive data while...
entry.summary: Burkov summarizes a security analysis of NVIDIA GPU confidential computing (GPU-CC) on H100, reconstructing its hardware/software components, initialization, and CPU-GPU runtime data paths to clarify guarantees and remaining risks of the proprietary system.

entry.title:
earlier this ~spring, models got good enough to drive browsers
in some ways, browsers are the new t...
entry.summary: Harrison Chase (LangChain) observes that models became good enough to drive browsers earlier this year, arguing browsers are the new terminal as a general-purpose agent tool, and points to a deep dive by Sydney Runkle on how they designed browser-driving tools for MDA.

entry.title: We’re releasing StateBench so researchers can test new models, extend our work, & build better s...
entry.summary: Allen AI announces the public release of StateBench, inviting researchers to test models, extend the work, and build better state-tracking datasets, with links to blog and dataset.

entry.title: Further evidence for what I keep saying - Anthropic’s Q2 was an anomaly, and all the projections bas...
entry.summary: Gary Marcus claims new evidence shows Anthropic's spectacular Q2 was an anomaly and that projections extrapolating from it were fantasy, consistent with his long-running skepticism about AI-company growth narratives.

entry.title: @MTHajiaghayi I, and I suspect many others, would be opposed to ceding human judgement, discretion, ...
entry.summary: Gautam Kamath argues against removing human judgment, discretion, and curation from the conference peer review process, apparently responding to a proposal in a thread about review automation.

entry.title: The “can LLMs do X better than Y can do X?” question has become increasingly meaningless, as the LLM...
entry.summary: Andrew White argues that comparisons asking whether LLMs can do X better than domain tool Y are increasingly meaningless, since the LLM can simply incorporate Y or something like it into its own toolkit.

entry.title: Long-context language-model systems are increasingly used for tasks such as document analysis and re...
entry.summary: Burkov summarizes a research paper proposing Time-to-Correct-Answer (TTCA), a metric capturing total delay including retries after wrong answers in long-context retrieval. The paper introduces LAAR, an accuracy-aware routing method tested across five models, 4K-64K token contexts, and three languages, outperforming load-aware and session-affinity routing.

entry.title:
This is for freelancers and anyone doing creative work.
This gives you an agent that takes care of ...
entry.summary: svpino describes an AI agent aimed at freelancers and creative professionals that automates routine business tasks: drafting client proposals, generating and scheduling tasks from project descriptions, sending client progress updates, preparing invoices, and maintaining time logs from task activity.

entry.title: StateBench separates state tracking into 4 levels: r-trivial, aperiodic, soluble, & general fini...
entry.summary: Allen AI explains StateBench's four difficulty levels of state tracking—r-trivial, aperiodic, soluble, and general finite—ranging from remembering fixed facts like a birth date to tracking a ball as cups are repeatedly swapped.

entry.title:
Decompiled and got the Wake Island map working now, which is more fun because it has planes!
I just...
entry.summary: levelsio announces he reverse-engineered and got the classic Wake Island map running in his open-source flight simulator, with multiplayer playable now and plans to add it to the main server rotation once tested.

entry.title: Baseten researcher @oneill_c explains why fully automating AI research may require something today's...
entry.summary: An MTSlive post quoting Baseten researcher Conor O'Neill arguing that fully automating AI research requires Einstein-level creativity LLMs lack: staying in the current paradigm yields diminishing returns and ever-harder RL environments, while paradigm shifts need intuition models have not shown; he also mocks recurring optimistic AI-research-automation predictions by comparing them to Elon Musk's self-driving timelines.

entry.title:
"Space is kind of the natural place to expand the energy real estate."
Cowboy Space CEO @BaijuBhatt...
entry.summary: MTS Live quotes Cowboy Space CEO Baiju Bhatt arguing that orbital solar energy could power AI data centers as terrestrial energy infrastructure and grid capacity become untenable amid political backlash against data centers.

entry.title: Even in bypass permissions mode, Claude Code still asks before a few especially risky rm commands. T...
entry.summary: Claude Code gains an env flag to skip even the last few risky rm prompts in throwaway containers, and timed-out shell commands now continue in the background so long builds or test suites are not killed mid-run.

entry.title:
💸 Update: My total biz expenses have now dropped to just ~$300/mo!
This is to run all my websites/a...
entry.summary: levelsio reports his total business expenses dropped to about $300/month to run websites serving 20,000 paying customers, 252 million visitors, and 2.4 billion requests per year (excluding an $8,000/month GPU and storage bill for Photo AI). He credits Claude Code with finding roughly $34,000/month in savings, including switching to cheaper video models and routing image jobs to cheaper cloud options, and reflects on AI-driven cost-cutting implications for the economy.

entry.title: Even a few months ago, you would get tons of nitpicks and useless comments, now you are far more lik...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick observes that frontier model feedback on intellectual work has improved markedly in recent months, shifting from nitpicks to substantive, deep critique resembling an eccentric but capable peer reviewer.

entry.title: - Paper 488 claims to prove P = NP. Paper 872 claims to prove P != NP. At least one is wrong! (My wa...
entry.summary: Kamath notes that among STOC 2027 public submissions, one paper claims to prove P = NP and another claims the opposite, wagering both are wrong; he also reports 339 single-author submissions and that about half of solo authors have never published at STOC/FOCS/SODA before.

entry.title: These are early steps, and we’re looking for engineers, engineering firms, and software partners to ...
entry.summary: OpenAI closes out its physical-world engineering thread by inviting engineers, engineering firms, and software partners to help shape what comes next.

entry.title: If an organization’s identity provider doesn’t support EMA, Claude can vouch for each signed-in memb...
entry.summary: Anthropic developer account explains a fallback for Enterprise Managed Auth: when an organization's identity provider does not support EMA, Claude itself can vouch for signed-in members, allowing eligible members to auto-connect to a plugin once an admin enables it.

entry.title:
Top stories in AI today:
- OpenAI’s Astra rewrites other AI from the inside - OpenAI grades its AI ...
entry.summary: The Rundown AI daily digest lists top AI stories: OpenAI's Astra reportedly rewriting other AI models from the inside, OpenAI benchmarking its models on everyday tasks, a Riverside tool for clipping interviews, and OpenAI joining Abu Dhabi's AI-native government initiative.

entry.title: Have GPUs in Kubernetes? NVIDIA AI Cluster Runtime brings together NVIDIA Dynamo and the infrastruct...
entry.summary: NVIDIA AI announces AI Cluster Runtime, which bundles Dynamo with tested infrastructure component versions and validation checks for GPU-based Kubernetes deployments, with a walkthrough and KubeCon North America presence.

entry.title: @natolambert Any AI Natives (Cursor, Decagon, etc.) that are multi-vendor inference (spread load bet...
entry.summary: Soumith Chintala replies to Nathan Lambert noting that AI-native companies like Cursor and Decagon that spread inference load across vendors such as Fireworks, Together, and Baseten likely account for a large chunk of aggregate token consumption numbers.

entry.title:
Specialized Models >> Larger Models.
This is an open-source platform that will help you choose and ...
entry.summary: Santiago Valdarrama promotes an open-source platform for routing tasks to specialized small models, e.g. using four different models to classify a message, read image text, search files, and write a response within one agent.

entry.title: Decision models are underrated
entry.summary: Arav Srinivas opines that decision models are underrated, in a short thesis-style statement.

entry.title: Strand Therapeutics CEO @DrSynbio explains how his team is using an encryption-like approach to make...

entry.title: Social Summary: November 03, 2026
entry.summary:
Research claims and evaluation debates dominated AI discussion. Ethan Mollick amplified a potentially landmark claim that GPT-6 Astra directly edited Qwen3.5-0.8B weights for math gains. Meanwhile, MIT CSAIL's OPAL used an AI agent that rewrites its own optimizer during training, and Ion Stoica's EAT evolved the agentic system itself for state-of-the-art results.

  • Anthropic drew huge engagement with its paid Residency launch and the Messages API threads beta; Claude Code integration cut first-token latency roughly 35% on very long requests
  • Benchmark skepticism ran strong: Mollick noted the GDPval successor lacks human baselines, Vik Paruchuri argued against public benchmark scores for model selection, and OpenAI's LifeVal refocused evaluation on everyday user tasks
  • Nathan Lambert argued open models win by driving inference costs down; Francois Chollet's critique of punchline-driven LLM prose resonated widely
  • Policy tensions rose as Rep. Whitesides called for a one-month frontier pause, and OpenAI reportedly added Dan Driscoll in a national security role
  • Practitioner sentiment: $200 plans feel worth it, agents underuse MCPs even when available per levelsio, whose Battlefield 1942 decompile showcased agentic coding power
entry.content:
Research claims and evaluation debates dominated AI discussion. Ethan Mollick amplified a potentially landmark claim that GPT-6 Astra directly edited Qwen3.5-0.8B weights for math gains. Meanwhile, MIT CSAIL's OPAL used an AI agent that rewrites its own optimizer during training, and Ion Stoica's EAT evolved the agentic system itself for state-of-the-art results.

  • Anthropic drew huge engagement with its paid Residency launch and the Messages API threads beta; Claude Code integration cut first-token latency roughly 35% on very long requests
  • Benchmark skepticism ran strong: Mollick noted the GDPval successor lacks human baselines, Vik Paruchuri argued against public benchmark scores for model selection, and OpenAI's LifeVal refocused evaluation on everyday user tasks
  • Nathan Lambert argued open models win by driving inference costs down; Francois Chollet's critique of punchline-driven LLM prose resonated widely
  • Policy tensions rose as Rep. Whitesides called for a one-month frontier pause, and OpenAI reportedly added Dan Driscoll in a national security role
  • Practitioner sentiment: $200 plans feel worth it, agents underuse MCPs even when available per levelsio, whose Battlefield 1942 decompile showcased agentic coding power

entry.title: If this holds up, it is big: "We asked GPT-6 Astra to edit Qwen3.5-0.8B weights to improve math. It ...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick amplifies a research blog claiming that GPT-6 Astra directly edited the weights of a small Qwen3.5-0.8B model — modifying only 0.016% of weights, without gradients or further training — fixing reasoning loops and improving math performance up to 6x and instruction following 3x. Mollick flags it with appropriate caution: if it holds up, it is big.

entry.title: Applications are now open for the Anthropic Residency, a paid, fixed-term research program for acade...
entry.summary: Anthropic announces that applications are open for its paid Residency program targeting academics, technical founders, and staff-level engineers interested in AI safety, with no ML background required and a November 22 deadline.

entry.title: When you think about the Labs' weird approach to software (sudden changes, bad communication), it is...
entry.summary: Mollick explains the labs' erratic software behavior and poor communication as stemming from a core belief that current products are temporary revenue-raising bridges until AGI renders all products obsolete.

entry.title:
Message threads are now in public beta on the Messages API.
The API caches your conversation on the...
entry.summary: Anthropic's developer account announces that message threads are entering public beta on the Messages API. The feature caches conversation state server-side between turns so clients send only new messages plus the previous message ID instead of resending the full history, reducing latency before Claude starts responding.

entry.title:
What if an optimizer could think & react while a neural network trains?
MIT researchers developed O...
entry.summary: MIT CSAIL announces OPAL, a deep learning optimizer powered by an AI agent that observes training dynamics and rewrites its own source code during training, improving performance on vision and language tasks, inventing specialized schedules, and developing strategies to prevent loss spikes and escape overfitting, with paper and code links provided.

entry.title: New talk on the open model economy. I wanted to break down the case of where open model builders sho...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert previews his talk 'How Open Models Win' for Fireworks Forge 2026, arguing open model builders should focus on driving inference costs down on specialized repetitive tasks rather than competing head-on with frontier labs on general agents. He maps the fragmented open model economy and the challenge of feeding application revenue back into the next model training cycle.

entry.title: The most grating aspect of LLM writing is that it tries to turn every single sentence into a punchli...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet criticizes LLM writing style, arguing that models try to turn every sentence into a punchline or witty slogan regardless of where emphasis belongs, calling it a tiring, overused formula.

entry.title: Nice to see a successor to GDPval to evaluate AI work but really needs human baselines like GDPval. ...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick reviews a new successor benchmark to OpenAI's GDPval for evaluating AI economic work, noting it lacks human baselines, that GPT-6 Pro identified grading errors in it, and that 0% scores mask meaningful differences in success rates, while still calling it valuable.

entry.title: For AGI to benefit all of humanity, it should help people with the everyday tasks that matter most t...
entry.summary: OpenAI introduces LifeVal, a new benchmark built from feedback of thousands of ChatGPT users about where they most want personal-assistant help, such as finding childcare, accessing government services, and managing finances. The lab says it has used the benchmark over the past year to measure and improve model performance on everyday tasks.

entry.title: We are collaborating with Silicon Data to bring market-based GPU pricing into AA-AgentPerf, our data...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces a collaboration with Silicon Data to incorporate market-based GPU rental pricing into their AA-AgentPerf datacenter benchmark, introducing a Throughput per $/hr metric using daily-updated price indices for H100, H200, B200, and B300; NVIDIA's B300 generally leads on value, with B200 matching at faster output speeds on some models.

entry.title: I decompiled probably my favorite game ever: Battlefield 1942 and I put it on the web with multiplay...
entry.summary: levelsio announces he decompiled Battlefield 1942 and ported it to the web with multiplayer, a far harder feat than prior Quake/DOOM ports because no open-source engine existed. Using Claude Opus 5.5 with Claude Code, the agent disassembled 57,000 x86 functions and translated them into C. The flagship post of the thread with ~112k views and 1,192 likes.

entry.title: Should you rely on public benchmark scores when choosing a model? @VikParuchuri argues "no" in this ...
entry.summary: Hamel Husain summarizes Vik Paruchuri's talk arguing against relying on public benchmark scores for model selection, cataloging concrete flaws in popular OCR benchmarks: ParseBench contains factually wrong expected values (310 vs 303 GW), chart tests asking for unprinted values, formatting tests contradicted by source documents, and scorer failures; olmOCR-bench penalizes correct line breaks and capitalization; and aggregate scores can rank models inversely to their actual content quality.

entry.title: one week in my takeaway is that you don't need unlimited tokens to do great work, the $200 plans are...
entry.summary: trq212 shares a one-week takeaway from using $200 AI subscription plans: you do not need unlimited tokens to do great work, the plans are amazing, and 'this is the most expensive intelligence will ever be'. The post went viral with 6.9k likes and 353k views.

entry.title: .@Rep_Whitesides warns we may already be entering the age of self-improving AI, and nobody knows wha...
entry.summary: A tweet quoting Rep. Whitesides arguing that recursive self-improvement (AI improving AI) may already be underway, citing Anthropic's reported highs in agent development usage, and describing legislative language directing CAISI to track frontier models capable of self-improvement without human oversight and to establish voluntary lab agreements for sharing metrics on automated R&D.

entry.title: New paper on compute-optimal scaling prescriptions for data constrained pre-training. Our prescripti...
entry.summary: Andrew Wilson announces a new paper on compute-optimal scaling for data-constrained pretraining, led by Ethan Baron, whose prescriptions include a return of ensembling and reveal pathologies in prior approaches.

entry.title: Factory's @luke_alvoeiro explains how Droid beat Anthropic's native Claude Code harness using the ex...
entry.summary: Factory's Luke Alvoeiro claims its Droid coding agent beats Anthropic's Claude Code harness on Terminal Bench 4 by 8 points using the identical Opus 5.5 model, also citing 17% better cost efficiency and 25% faster execution. The platform's heaviest-used models are Opus 5.5 at high reasoning and GPT-6.1 Sol at high reasoning.

entry.title: The thing is that their products are unreasonably effective & getting better all the time becaus...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick argues AI lab products improve rapidly because the underlying LLMs do, which has rewarded labs for treating their consumer products as disposable rather than maintaining traditional software lifecycles.

entry.title: What if you evolved the AI agentic system itself? You could achieve SOTA results on some of the hard...
entry.summary: Ion Stoica (UC Berkeley) announces EAT, an approach that evolves the AI agentic system itself, reporting state-of-the-art results on difficult kernel optimization tasks.

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: OpenAI has appointed Dan Driscoll as Senior Counsellor for National Security Mod...
entry.summary: MTS Live reports breaking news, citing the Financial Times, that OpenAI has appointed Dan Driscoll as Senior Counsellor for National Security Modernisation, signaling deepening ties between OpenAI and national security institutions.

entry.title: @BobClowdr @heyshrutimishra Humans mostly do not think in words. Animals certainly don't think in w...
entry.summary: Yann LeCun argues that humans and animals do not think in words; language is a discrete representation of thought whose discreteness aids storage and memory, creating the illusion of verbal thinking. He also deflects the claim that nothing has happened in his research in five years by pointing to recent talks and papers.

entry.title: Again, @SemiAnalysis_ is doing something valuable here & you can see why benchmarks of expert-le...
entry.summary: Mollick praises a new SemiAnalysis expert-level work benchmark as valuable, noting it arrives at a time when major benchmarks like ARC-AGI, GDPval, and METR Long Tasks are saturated.

entry.title: We recently integrated message threads in Claude Code. On requests with 500K to 1M tokens, median ti...
entry.summary: Claude Devs reports that integrating message threads into Claude Code cut median time to first token by roughly 35% for 500K-1M token requests and shrank median long-conversation request size from ~800 KB to 1.8 KB.

entry.title: Turn a daytime drive into a rainy night while keeping the same road layout and vehicle trajectories....
entry.summary: NVIDIA AI highlights new Cosmos simulation recipes that transform daytime driving footage into rainy night conditions while preserving road layout and trajectories, aimed at generating data and testing policies for autonomous vehicles, robots, and surgical applications.

entry.title: I may or may have not just decompiled Battlefield 1942's raw C engine with Claude Code to run it in ...
entry.summary: @levelsio announces he apparently decompiled Battlefield 1942's raw C engine using Claude Code (Anthropic's AI coding assistant) to run the game in the browser.

entry.title:
"I've called for a one-month pause on frontier model development." – @Rep_Whitesides
The Congressma...

Whitesides calling for a one-month pause on frontier model development, drawing an analogy to aerospace industry safety stoppages from his NASA and Virgin Galactic background, referencing an OpenAI pause after a Hugging Face incident, and arguing government impetus is needed given the accelerating power of models.

entry.title: NOMENCLATURE WATCH: Just got my first email from OpenAI referring to their data centers as 'compute ...
entry.summary: Casey Newton flags that OpenAI has started calling its data centers compute campuses in email communications, a nomenclature observation with industry-significance implications.

entry.title: Factory's @luke_alvoeiro explains why AI coding agents are wasting massive amounts of tokens on info...
entry.summary: Factory's Luke Alvoeiro explains how programmatic tool calling lets coding agents run commands but only receive results they explicitly request, avoiding massive context bloat — e.g., moving 150 Linear tickets where only the success/failure outcome matters. He argues token efficiency extends agent runtimes and preserves long-term coherence.

entry.title: To use it, add the thread parameter and beta header to your requests. It's available on the Claude P...
entry.summary: Anthropic's developer account explains how to enable the new message-threads feature via a thread parameter and beta header, noting availability across Claude Platform, AWS, Microsoft Foundry, and Google Cloud at standard token rates.

entry.title:
My friend @stevelacey says AI agents almost never use MCPs if they have it available
I thought the ...
entry.summary: levelsio shares an observation that AI agents rarely use MCP servers even when available, arguing MCPs and API endpoints will likely merge long-term; he adds MCPs to his sites mainly because users expect them. High engagement: ~74k views, 348 likes, 104 replies.

entry.title:
I never know what to say when people talk about the “GPU spot market”.
Some clouds have preemptible...
entry.summary: Stefan Bernhardsson (Modal) breaks down why 'GPU spot market' is a misleading term: AWS spot prices move slowly with demand, GCP uses monthly prices, Azure uses fixed discounts, some neoclouds like Nebius auction capacity, and vendors like SpaceX sell short-term non-preemptible capacity. He argues there is no liquid marketplace and preemptibility is conflated, capping it with an Inglourious Basterds meme reference.

entry.title: Larridin CEO @rfradin says AI is creating 100X engineers while turning other employees into "human s...
entry.summary: Larridin's CEO argues AI has settled the 10X engineer debate, producing 50-100X engineers for roughly 10% of employees while making the bottom 25% less productive, coining the term human slop cannons. He also highlights under-monetized Anthropic enterprise revenue and urges investment in training and organizational transformation rather than layoffs.

entry.title: Tutor Intelligence CEO @joshgruenstein explains how GPT Astra can generate robotics simulations that...
entry.summary: Tutor Intelligence's CEO describes how OpenAI's GPT Astra generates robotics simulation environments that previously required entire teams of simulation engineers, praising its spatial reasoning. He notes Opus 5.5 showed similar capabilities, suggesting all major labs post-train on spatial data, while cautioning that sim-to-real gap closure still requires real robots.

entry.title: NEW: An MIT CSAIL team found GPT-6 Astra can improve some AI models by rewriting their weights itsel...
entry.summary: The Rundown AI reports that an MIT CSAIL team found GPT-6 Astra can improve other AI models by directly rewriting their weights, with a single edit raising a small Qwen model's math score from 7.9% to 48.1%.

entry.title: OpenAI says it wants ChatGPT handling your life admin, so it built LifeVal, a test of real chores pi...
entry.summary: The Rundown AI reports on LifeVal, an OpenAI benchmark of real-world chores built from time-use studies and a 3,995-person poll, where GPT-6 Astra scored 100% on 10 of 16 tasks (e.g., finding a lost engagement ring match, quitting email lists) and averaged 80.6% overall.

entry.title: .@Rep_Whitesides explains why the US is spending a fraction of what the UK spends on AI safety, desp...
entry.summary: Quotes from Rep. Whitesides criticizing the US underfunding of AI safety relative to the UK, noting bipartisan support to raise funding to 80-100 million dollars and arguing the US needs a competent, funded government regulator regardless of one's views on AI.

entry.title: In updating a graphic showing U.S. company AI adoption over time according to a long-running U.S. Ce...
entry.summary: Simon Willison reports that while updating a graphic of US company AI adoption from a long-running Census Bureau survey, he found the Bureau's work has been affected by the recently introduced Super Intelligence executive order, linking his writeup.

entry.title: I had Opus 5.5 create a site where you can see the fastest routes into every city in the US, figure ...
entry.summary: Mollick showcases a website built with Claude Opus 5.5 that visualizes fastest routes into US cities, fairest meetup points in America, and city watersheds, inspired by the defunct Arterial Mapping project.

entry.title:
This is a new streaming decision model:
• Give it text + list of questions • It answers back with a...
entry.summary: @svpino describes a new streaming decision/extraction model that takes text plus a list of questions, returns answers with confidence scores that update in real time as text arrives (3x faster), and doubles as an extraction model (~150 ms per extraction) claimed to be 75x cheaper than Opus 5.5 for document extraction, all via a single endpoint with 20M free tokens offered.

entry.title:
This is an open-source tool that will let you carry knowledge between different coding assistants.
...
entry.summary: @svpino highlights an open-source tool that transfers knowledge across different coding assistants. The tool records coding sessions and converts useful fixes, corrections, and workflows into lessons that other coding assistants can then use, which he notes is especially handy when switching tools after hitting a usage limit.

entry.title:
A very tragic crash with a private jet once again
Before this crash the Learjet 60 was had fatal od...
entry.summary: Levelsio analyzes the safety statistics of a recent private jet crash involving a Learjet 60, comparing its fatal odds (1 in 1.1 million trips before the crash, now 1 in 800,000) to commercial airlines like Delta (1 in 25-40 million). He argues private aviation is inherently less safe due to lower pilot flight-hour requirements, less regulation, smaller airports without instrument landing systems, and weather vulnerability such as icing, while noting Gulfstream models retain flawless records.

entry.title: Larridin CEO @rfradin explains why an engineer spending $10,000 a month on AI isn't necessarily more...
entry.summary: Larridin's CEO discusses why token spend is a poor proxy for engineering productivity: an engineer spending $10k/month on tokens is not automatically better than one spending $1k. Real measurement requires looking at what fraction of AI-generated code is valuable, reaches production, avoids rollback, or is slop code, and must be evaluated department by department.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: A Hangzhou startup says its open-weight AI model beats OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra at ...
entry.summary: A breakdown of a claim by Hangzhou startup Deep Principle that its open-weight model Hydrogen-1.0, fine-tuned from Z.ai's open GLM-5.3 on the lab's internal research records, scores 38.3% vs GPT-6 Astra's 33.3% on OpenAI's own FrontierScience-Research benchmark and 93% on GPQA Diamond, at GLM-5.3 API pricing. Includes a quoted comment on the value of training on full lab notebooks including failed attempts.

entry.title: When you think about the Labs' weird approach to software releases (sudden changes, bad communicatio...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick contextualizes AI labs' odd release practices — sudden changes and poor communication — as stemming from a core belief that current products are temporary revenue vehicles until true AGI renders all products obsolete.

entry.title: Tutor Intelligence CEO @joshgruenstein explains the 3 major bottlenecks preventing robots from scali...
entry.summary: Tutor Intelligence's CEO lays out bottlenecks to robot scaling in US factories: after 60 years of dumb repetitive machines, the US deployed only 38,000 industrial robots in 2025 against a million unfilled manufacturing/logistics jobs; robots that cannot do the jobs leave no installed base of bodies; and companies must simultaneously train models, build hardware, and deploy.

entry.summary: Mollick highlights that AI adoption keeps growing, contrasting with mid-2025 narratives that adoption was dropping, and points to a post by Simon discussing methodology changes.

entry.title: In AA-PersonalityBench, Kimi K3.1 Pro shows the biggest personality change we’ve seen compared to a ...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports that Kimi K3.1 Pro shows the largest personality shift versus a direct predecessor they have measured: an average 30-point movement across 30 traits versus Kimi K3, with 18 of 30 traits moving 25 or more percentile points; the next largest was 23 points from GPT-6 Sol to GPT-6.1 Sol.

entry.summary: Ethan Mollick argues AI lab products keep improving because the underlying LLMs keep improving, and that labs have been rewarded for treating their products as disposable since LLM improvement broke conventional software release cycles.

entry.summary: @svpino describes a new decision model for audio that takes raw audio plus a list of questions and outputs answers with confidence scores, analyzing audio directly without transcription, notably able to answer based on tone, hesitation, laughter, and other paralinguistic cues absent from transcripts.

entry.summary: AI Now Institute shares a recorded discussion from the People's AI Assembly co-hosted with More Perfect Union, featuring Bhairavi Desai (NYTWA), Lorena Gonzalez, Noam Scheiber, and Jasmine Sun. Desai argues for class conscious unionism in the context of AI's labor impacts.

entry.title:
Btw, I used 0 MCPs 😬
Sandboxed CLI or OpenAPI.yaml, that's all your agent needs.
entry.summary: Théophile Dinh claims he built his agent with zero MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers, arguing that a sandboxed CLI or an OpenAPI.yaml spec is all an agent needs — a contrarian take on the MCP ecosystem standard.

entry.title: Modern LLMs achieve remarkable capabilities, yet the mathematical principles governing how they repr...
entry.summary: Burkov summarizes a research article arguing that LLMs lack an adequate theoretical foundation, which hampers anticipating jailbreaks and misalignment and limits architecture design. The paper demonstrates that language models exhibit an architecture-agnostic low-rank structure over long token sequences, and explores how this property can be exploited for generation and analysis.

Tested with SALMONN 13B on 160K audio examples and evaluated on MMAU and MMAR benchmarks against several baselines.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 02, 2026
entry.summary:
Agentic AI workflows dominated the day. Andrej Karpathy's HackerTube — built by filtering 43M Hacker News comments with Claude — was the viral centerpiece, and swyx flagged that he used medium reasoning effort with Opus 5.5. levelsio extended the theme by having Claude Code autonomously edit a drone vlog, showing agents working beyond pure software.

  • Yann LeCun argued LLMs' large parameter counts reflect stored declarative knowledge, contrasting his JEPA world-model architecture
  • François Chollet framed evolution as optimizing generality and robustness over benchmark-style specialization
  • Ethan Mollick quantified the capability leap — from GPT-4's 4 minutes of autonomous work to multi-week task completion today — and praised GPT-6 Astra Pro for complex one-shot reasoning
  • Hamel Husain compared AI benchmark firms to Gartner and credit-rating agencies, sparking debate over conflicts of interest in model evaluation
  • Security discussion spiked around an active MPTCP vulnerability, with levelsio urging fully closed VPS ports using Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel
  • Concern over AI reply-bot 'slop' grew: Mollick documented evolving slop-bots in his replies, while others built automated blocklists
entry.content:

Andrej Karpathy's HackerTube — built by filtering 43M Hacker News comments with Claude — was the viral centerpiece, and swyx flagged that he used medium reasoning effort with Opus 5.5. levelsio extended the theme by having Claude Code autonomously edit a drone vlog, showing agents working beyond pure software.

  • Yann LeCun argued LLMs' large parameter counts reflect stored declarative knowledge, contrasting his JEPA world-model architecture
  • François Chollet framed evolution as optimizing generality and robustness over benchmark-style specialization
  • Ethan Mollick quantified the capability leap — from GPT-4's 4 minutes of autonomous work to multi-week task completion today — and praised GPT-6 Astra Pro for complex one-shot reasoning
  • Hamel Husain compared AI benchmark firms to Gartner and credit-rating agencies, sparking debate over conflicts of interest in model evaluation
  • Security discussion spiked around an active MPTCP vulnerability, with levelsio urging fully closed VPS ports using Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel

entry.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 4...
entry.summary: Karpathy announces HackerTube, a weekend project in which Claude filtered 43M comments across 20 years of Hacker News down to 6,454 repeatedly recommended videos, producing a curated viewing site built in roughly two hours with Opus 5.5 via Claude Code, including no-login state, natural thumbnails, released underlying data, and details of his mostly conversational build process.

entry.title: @heyshrutimishra LLMs accumulate a lot of declarative knowledge. That's how they can answer a large ...
entry.summary: Yann LeCun argues LLMs store large amounts of declarative knowledge, which is why they need so many parameters and memory, whereas JEPA world models replace knowledge accumulation with understanding, enabling usefulness with far less memory and training data; he summarizes a paper showing that shared anti-collapse criteria like SIGReg or VCReg make the encoder's representation geometry determined by the data's similarity structure.

entry.title:
GPT-4 could do 4 minutes of independent work with a 50% chance of success.
Current models can do mu...
entry.summary: Mollick quantifies capability growth: GPT-4 could handle about 4 minutes of autonomous work at 50% success, while current models sustain multiple weeks of agentic work; he dates the start of practical agentic work to around January 2026 and says earlier productivity gains were mostly confined to coding.

entry.title: Evolution doesn't benchmaxx. It optimizes for generality and robustness, because overspecialization ...
entry.summary: Chollet argues that evolution optimizes for generality and robustness rather than benchmark-style overfitting, since overspecialization makes species fragile when environments shift — an implicit critique of benchmaxxing in AI development.

entry.title:
My vlog today was fully edited by Claude Code with Opus 5.5!
I copied the video clips from my DJI t...
entry.summary: Indie developer @levelsio describes an end-to-end AI-assisted video editing workflow where Claude Code running Opus 5.5 autonomously edited his DJI drone footage into a 10-minute vlog. The pipeline combined mlx-whisper for on-device transcription, contact-sheet frame grids for visual understanding, SpeechBrain ECAPA for speaker voice matching, OpenCV with YuNet face detection for thumbnails, and Pillow for captions, with the final edit represented as a JSON list of cuts that the model selected itself. He notes he did not request or even know about most of the technical choices the agent made.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 01, 2026
entry.summary:
Agent engineering practice dominated discussion. Svpino, swyx, and Harrison Chase converged on a maturing discipline: deterministic tests over prose instructions, generate-then-critique loops over max-effort prompting, and signs that agent engineering is standardizing.

  • Andrew Wilson's (Berkeley) critique of mechanistic interpretability as a 'bait-and-switch' sparked the sharpest research-field debate; Yann LeCun added technical threads on nonlinearity pathologies and drew attention with criticism of Anthropic
  • Real-world agent deployments advanced on multiple fronts: NVIDIA agents steering the Allen Telescope Array for SETI/Breakthrough Listen, and Google DeepMind's PlanAssist cutting UK planning assessment times
  • Ethan Mollick posted timely evaluations of the GPT-6 Pro tier and a Halloween Claude Opus 5.5 ghost-census demo; Jerry Liu's boobench benchmark exposed repeating-character failures in LLMs and OCR tools
  • Levelsio's viral Europe tax thread (2.3M views on France's per-GB levy, Germany's AI tax, Italy's exit tax) energized Europe-vs-US sentiment, though specific claims remain unverified
  • Francois Chollet's reflection on dopamine and reward prediction error resonated widely with the RL community
entry.content:
Agent engineering practice dominated discussion. Svpino, swyx, and Harrison Chase converged on a maturing discipline: deterministic tests over prose instructions, generate-then-critique loops over max-effort prompting, and signs that agent engineering is standardizing.

  • Andrew Wilson's (Berkeley) critique of mechanistic interpretability as a 'bait-and-switch' sparked the sharpest research-field debate; Yann LeCun added technical threads on nonlinearity pathologies and drew attention with criticism of Anthropic
  • Real-world agent deployments advanced on multiple fronts: NVIDIA agents steering the Allen Telescope Array for SETI/Breakthrough Listen, and Google DeepMind's PlanAssist cutting UK planning assessment times
  • Ethan Mollick posted timely evaluations of the GPT-6 Pro tier and a Halloween Claude Opus 5.5 ghost-census demo; Jerry Liu's boobench benchmark exposed repeating-character failures in LLMs and OCR tools
  • Levelsio's viral Europe tax thread (2.3M views on France's per-GB levy, Germany's AI tax, Italy's exit tax) energized Europe-vs-US sentiment, though specific claims remain unverified
  • Francois Chollet's reflection on dopamine and reward prediction error resonated widely with the RL community

entry.title: Mechanistic interpretability was a huge missed opportunity. Many people wanted to join that effort, ...
entry.summary: Andrew Wilson argues that mechanistic interpretability became a bait-and-switch: people expected a broad study of generalization but got a narrow, esoteric focus on individual neurons, sparse autoencoders, influence functions, and saliency maps, calling it a waste.

entry.title: AI agents are now steering the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California to search for possible a...
entry.summary: NVIDIA AI announces that AI agents are steering the Allen Telescope Array for the SETI Institute and Breakthrough Listen to search for alien signals, using NVIDIA Holoscan and CUDA-X libraries, framed with a Halloween joke.

entry.title:
Deterministic tests > Written instructions
Anything that should be checked automatically should hav...
entry.summary: Svpino argues that deterministic checks beat written instructions when working with AI coding agents: enforce behavior with tests, formatters, type checkers, schema validation, regression tests and security scans rather than wasting tokens telling an agent to follow rules.

entry.title: The Pro series of GPT models continues to be really impressive for one-shot problems that involve co...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick praises the GPT-6 Pro tier for one-shot problems involving complex calculations, references, and sophisticated ideas, noting it is slow but delivers an oracle-like experience.

entry.title: The market for software migration from legacy systems has been limited to $30B a year or so because ...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick observes that the legacy software migration market has been capped at roughly $30B annually because migrations are expensive and maintenance is the safer default. Based on conversations with older firms, he reports that a backlog of scoped, cheaper migration projects is now being unlocked surprisingly quickly by AI.

entry.summary: swyx argues that a low-effort generation plus critique loop outperforms maximum-effort single-shot prompting, and links to a babysit-runs skill repo, positioning it as a technique for throughput-constrained agent workloads.

entry.title:
happy halloween! 🎃
we made a fun benchmark to "scare" LLMs and OCR tools into output repeating char...
entry.summary: Jerry Liu (LlamaIndex founder) announces a Halloween-themed benchmark called boobench that tests how LLMs and OCR tools fail on documents containing repeating characters, a real-world failure mode where models go off the rails. Includes links to the benchmark and dataset.

entry.title: We built PlanAssist to help UK Government planning officers speed up building and renovations across...
entry.summary: Google DeepMind announces PlanAssist, built with Gemini, which reportedly cuts UK planning officers' time assessing householder applications by up to 58% and is expanding to 12 more councils.

entry.title: Dopamine does not spike highest for guaranteed rewards. It spikes highest at reward prediction error...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet explains that dopamine spikes correlate with reward prediction error rather than guaranteed reward, drawing a life lesson that embracing risk and uncertainty increases enjoyment.

entry.title: A lot of content engineering challenges have pretty standard solutions, which has lead to some engin...
entry.summary: Harrison Chase observes that many content engineering challenges now have standard solutions, leading some engineers to call agent engineering solved or boring, but argues a new set of interesting challenges is emerging as agents evolve.

entry.title: Inspired by the spinor nature of spin–orbit-coupled electronic states, we introduce eSpinor, an SU(2...
entry.summary: Anima Anandkumar announces eSpinor, an SU(2)-equivariant graph neural network that propagates spinor features to predict spin-orbit coupling-dependent magnetic properties, aiming to replace costly CASSCF-SO multireference calculations in materials design for single-molecule magnets and MRI probes.

entry.title: Yeah, I've found that - the best current models are so good at reading code that simply deleting out...

entry.title: Unified multimodal models can both interpret and create images, but they usually produce a result in...
entry.summary: Andriy Burkov summarizes a research article on UniT, a framework that trains a unified multimodal model to plan, inspect, and iteratively refine its outputs over multiple rounds of reasoning and image editing. The researchers built about 12,000 filtered multi-step reasoning and editing examples using other models as generators and critics, fine-tuned the Bagel model on this data, and showed that added inference-time computation improves performance on image generation, compositional and multi-turn editing, and visual reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: Social Summary: October 31, 2026
entry.summary:
Anthropic's Boris Cherny dominated product news by removing the 5-hour limit for verified Ultra accounts, while OpenAI launched Private Intelligence enterprise controls. Perplexity CEO Arav Srinivas drew major attention with early evals calling Gemini 4 Carbon the strongest long-form research model tested, days after launch.

  • Bret Taylor revealed Sierra passed $400M ARR, doubling in five months — fueling bullish sentiment on the agent economy
  • Edison Scientific's Sam Rodriques showcased the Robin agent's Nature-published blindness treatment discovery, energizing AI-for-science discussion
  • Epoch AI's Alex Barry warned AI can weaponize Firefox patches within hours using GLM 5.3, sparking security anxiety
  • Ethan Mollick tallied rapid OpenAI product shutdowns, tempering launch hype with lifecycle realism
  • Cohere's Joelle Pineau argued frontier models are overkill for most enterprises and defended Canada's AI ambitions
  • Nathan Lambert and Harrison Chase led technical discourse on score-centering RL details and reframing agent observability

Overall sentiment: optimism about agent commercial traction and scientific breakthroughs, balanced by rising concern over AI-enabled cyberattacks and AI slop degrading online platforms.
entry.content:

  • Epoch AI's Alex Barry warned AI can weaponize Firefox patches within hours using GLM 5.3, sparking security anxiety
  • Ethan Mollick tallied rapid OpenAI product shutdowns, tempering launch hype with lifecycle realism
  • Cohere's Joelle Pineau argued frontier models are overkill for most enterprises and defended Canada's AI ambitions
  • Nathan Lambert and Harrison Chase led technical discourse on score-centering RL details and reframing agent observability

entry.title: Real-time translation must balance speed against accuracy: translating early reduces delay, but inco...
entry.summary: Andriy Burkov shares an article on simultaneous/cascaded speech translation. The work proposes a training method that generates 'stable' partial translations by comparing translations of progressively longer source prefixes against the full-sentence translation, keeping only agreeing target text. These examples are used to fine-tune Qwen3-8B, and the resulting system is evaluated translating English into German, Japanese, and Chinese. The core motivation is letting the model learn adaptively when it is safe to translate, replacing fixed timing policies that ignore per-phrase uncertainty.
